experiment: P11 single-node versus two-node prompt probe cost
source_cases: the same 72 consumed, unclipped prompt-permutation cases from P11 development

arms.single_calibrated: one complete node, prompt 1/2/3, 6 budget, required_complete_nodes=1
arms.single_fixed: same one-node probe state and continuation targets, then prompt 1
arms.double_calibrated: two complete nodes, prompt 1/2/3 on each, 12 budget, required_complete_nodes=2
arms.double_fixed: same two-node probe state and continuation targets, then prompt 1

comparisons: single_calibrated versus single_fixed isolates prompt identification at equal cost
double_calibrated versus double_fixed isolates prompt identification at equal cost
single_calibrated versus double_calibrated measures net exploration-cost difference but also reflects one-node versus verified evidence

controls.continuation: within each probe-count pair, target schedule is identical and fixed before prompt-ID execution
controls.prompt_configs: all six permutations of [15,10,-5], three wide rotations and three close rotations

required_reporting: probe budget and continuation action count
paired terminal means and complete loss lists for all three comparisons
results remain development evidence and do not change the selected runtime probe count
